intro.text: The main religion of eastern Roshar: belief in one god, the Almighty, and the Ten Heralds he anointed to protect mankind in their endless fight against the Voidbringers.

description.text: Ardents are slaves to high-ranking lighteyes and believe the Almighty set these limits so they never rise above their station. Lighteyes are thought to hold more innate Glory.

The Almighty is held to be the force of good and creator of mankind, the Dawnsingers, animals, plants and Roshar itself. Ten is his number: ten holy names, ten Heralds and a ten-faced crystal that stands for him.
Each Vorin chooses a Calling and a Glory, an attribute of the Almighty to emulate. Those best at their Calling join the Heralds after death in the fight to retake the Tranquiline Halls.
Vorins pray with glyphwards, written prayers that are burned to send their souls to the Almighty.
Traditional temples are circular and domed, usually exactly ten feet high, and filled with statues and pictures of the Heralds.

items.text: Vorinism's origins are lost, but the name Almighty was used even by the Heralds. Nohadon's The Way of Kings was one of its early holy texts.
In Old Vorinism the Knights Radiant were part of the faith, and how one lived mattered more than what one achieved. Ardents could own land and property.
After the Recreance the Knights Radiant came to be seen as traitors. Focus moved to texts such as Arts and Majesty, bringing the Vorin divide between men and women.
Under the Hierocracy the ardents controlled what people could know, claiming sole authority to interpret scripture and the Almighty's will, while claiming to foresee the future themselves.

The Hierocracy's size became its weakness. The warlord Sadees, the Sunmaker, made war on it, splitting the ardentia into devotaries; ardents lost their land and their freedom and became slaves to lighteyes.

Sadees claimed the ardents' visions were fabrications. Seeking the future became heresy, ardents became advisors rather than authorities, and each person was to find the faith's meaning for themselves.
Sadees's conquest reached as far west as Azir, but Vorinism never took hold there. The lands once under the Hierocracy remain the Vorin kingdoms.
